title: What is known about 1RB0LB_1RC1LE_1LD0RF_---1LB_0LA0LC_1LB1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LB_1RC1LE_1LD0RF_---1LB_0LA0LC_1LB1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves two crossings the run uses and the situations that lead to a halt (kernel), and no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in 109 steps.

What it does. The head sweeps the whole tape. The background is the alternating word 1010…, broken every few cells by a defect (00, 11, 111, …). The sweeps move the background past the head unchanged in shape (A carrying a 1 turns 01 into 10; B turns 0101 into 1010) and rearrange the defects; their pattern has no visible order.
Where a halt would come from. Only D reading a 0 halts; D is entered from C reading a 0, so 0 C>0 halts. In 2·108 steps D always reads a 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: E with 0 two left, 0 left, 1 under the head. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 47,969 cells have been visited and 30,160 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.492).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: A with a 1 behind it turns each 01 into 10 going right (eight steps a copy); B with 11 ahead turns each 0101 into 1010 going left (22 steps a copy).

claims.title: The halting situations
claims.text: 0 C>0 halts after one step, 0 0 E>1 after two, 0 0 1 B>1 after three, 0 0 A>0 1 after four.

claims.title: D never reads a 0 in 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps
claims.text: In the first 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps the machine is in state D 7,101,514 times, every time on a 1: the halting transition D0 is never close to firing in a way the run shows.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 24, history 1 up to width 24, history 2 up to width 24, history 3 up to width 24, LRU history up to width 8 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 20, p = 3 up to width 20, p = 4 up to width 20, p = 6 up to width 20. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..8; n = 9 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The defects behave chaotically; NGramCPS with n ≤ 10 and window CTL with K ≤ 7 leave it open.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine sweeps over a tape of alternating 1s and 0s full of small defects, and the defects move around without visible order. This page runs it in your browser.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 47,969 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: An alternating background
html: Most of the tape reads 1 0 1 0 …. Sweeping right, A with a 1 behind it shifts the pattern by one cell as it passes, eight steps per pair:

(Lean: walk_A.) Sweeping left, B with 1 1 ahead turns each 0101 into 1010 (walk_B). Where the alternation breaks, at a 00 or 11, the head does something else, and these defects are what changes from sweep to sweep.

sections.heading: D must read a 0
html: Only D reading a 0 halts, and D is entered from C reading a 0 and moving left. So two 0s in a row under C halt the machine:
D is entered 7.1 million times in the first 2·108 steps, always on a 1.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.492).
After 109 steps the tape spans 47,969 cells (26,418 left of the start, 8,635 right), with a density of 1s of 0.629.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Two-sided bouncer on a tape of alternating 1 0 1 0 stretches broken by short defects (00, 11, 111); the defects move and multiply irregularly. Open.
family: alternating background with disordered defects (two-sided bouncer)
